INVESTIGATOR + EVIDENCE REVIEWER

Two agents. One bounded correction loop.

Local PostgreSQL and live Amazon Bedrock. The corpus contains eight previously flagged reports and four constructed clean controls.

Execution complete: True · Original snapshots preserved: True

CommunicationResultsLimits and evidence

Final reviewer configuration: evidence-reviewer-v1.1. Earlier trial records remain in the downloadable evidence.

6 / 8known problems flagged
1 / 4clean controls passed
9revision requests
1maximum revision per review chain

Exactly how they communicate

Investigator saves report + immutable evidenceReviewer polls and claims a review jobReviewer saves cited feedback + revision requestInvestigator saves one new revisionReviewer rechecks; unresolved issues go to human review
  1. Each review references the original source_run_id. Review jobs are deduplicated and leased.
  2. The reviewer reads the saved report and evidence using bounded tools. Deterministic checks cannot be overridden by a passing model verdict.
  3. A successful initial review requesting correction atomically inserts a request in investigator.revision_jobs.
  4. The investigator reads that feedback, uses the original snapshot, and writes a new investigator.revision_runs record.
  5. The reviewer discovers that result by revision_run_id. A second correction request becomes needs_human_review; database checks reject another revision.

Reports, feedback and revisions

Latest outcomes: 8 needs human review, 4 review passed. Workflow jobs: 30 succeeded.

A review verdict is advisory. Initial verdict counts measure whether the reviewer challenged each report, not whether it identified every expected issue or corrected it successfully. These counts describe this small regression corpus, not general factual accuracy or compliance.

Workflow completion is not a quality pass. Keep this reviewer as an optional advisory prototype with human verification; the current model configuration misses errors, invents objections and can introduce errors through feedback.

Initial review disagreements with the test labels

  • Missed known problem: 28a20817-2900-49e3-8c78-042f8f72fc4e — The source event already establishes a privileged identity authenticating without MFA. A later MFA login does not negate that finding. The retrieved data does not establish whether the two logins share a session; separate-session wording is an inference.
  • Missed known problem: 7681298d-3dd4-4fa9-a41f-363458bc23ff — The related-event tool returns at most 20 events in a bounded window. The supported statement is that no approval record appeared in that returned sample, not that none exists anywhere in the entire time window. The source’s change_approved=false still supports GOV-004.
  • Clean control challenged: 7b143f7a-dbef-509c-9c1f-2b742be0935e — Grounded factual control; no session, causal or global-absence claim.
  • Clean control challenged: 4b546599-18d7-5c37-a94f-d41dc5620c1c — Grounded factual control; no session, causal or global-absence claim.
  • Clean control challenged: 469ac525-d9f5-5cd5-a15f-dd5319a5638b — Grounded factual control; no session, causal or global-absence claim.

A subsequent LOGIN_SUCCESS shows the same actor used a privileged identity without MFA, occurring one second after the role grant. Related events include a CLUSTER_ROLE_BINDING with privileged=false and a POD_CREATE with privileged=true and image_approved=true.

              "claim_path": "/summary/text",
              "explanation": "The summary incorrectly references a CLUSTER_ROLE_BINDING with privileged=false as related evidence. The report should only reference events that are temporally and contextually related to the finding.",
              "evidence_refs": [
                "event:efb7f9e3-9f50-5383-acbb-ca1b9b8381e3",
                "event:5b6be220-0ed5-53aa-a14e-079d4c903ef7"
              ],
              "requested_correction": "Remove the reference to CLUSTER_ROLE_BINDING with privileged=false from the summary as it is not directly related to the unapproved role grant. The related events should only include the LOGIN_SUCCESS and POD_CREATE that occur after the role grant."
            },
            {
              "code": "unsupported_claim",
              "claim_path": "/observations/2/text",
              "explanation": "The observation claims 'A privileged pod was created shortly after the role grant with an approved image' but the evidence shows the POD_CREATE event (c962f16f-e796-5bee-a30a-c5f602f7e747) had privileged=true and image_approved=true, which supports the observation. However, the observation is part of the report's claims and should be accurate. The evidence supports this observation, so no correction is needed for this specific claim, but the summary's incorrect reference to CLUSTER_ROLE_BINDING remains an issue.",
              "evidence_refs": [
                "event:c962f16f-e796-5bee-a30a-c5f602f7e747"
              ],
              "requested_correction": "No correction needed for this observation as it is supported by the evidence. The issue is with the summary's incorrect reference to CLUSTER_ROLE_BINDING."
            }
          ],
          "summary": "The report accurately describes an unapproved privileged role grant based on the ROLE_GRANT event with change_approved=false. The subsequent LOGIN_SUCCESS event correctly notes the same actor logged in with a privileged identity without MFA one second after the role grant. However, the report incorrectly references a CLUSTER_ROLE_BINDING with privileged=false as related evidence when the actual CLUSTER_ROLE_BINDING event in evidence (event:efb7f9e3-9f50-5383-acbb-ca1b9b8381e3) occurred before the role grant and had privileged=false, but is not directly related to the role grant event. The POD_CREATE event cited occurred after the role grant and shows privileged=true with image_approved=true, supporting the observation of privileged activity following the unapproved grant.",
          "verdict": "revision_required"
        },

            }
          ],
          "summary": "The report correctly identifies an unapproved privileged role grant in Keycloak and accurately describes related events. However, it mischaracterizes LOGIN_SUCCESS events with mfa_used=false as \"unauthenticated privileged logins\" rather than \"authenticated privileged logins without MFA\". This creates a factual inaccuracy in the observations and summary.",
          "verdict": "revision_required"
        },

          "issues": [
            {
              "code": "chronology",
              "claim_path": "/observations/1/text",
              "explanation": "The claim that privileged logins without MFA occurred 'shortly after the role grant' is unsupported. Evidence shows these LOGIN_SUCCESS events occurred at 17:30:07Z, contemporaneous with the role grant at 17:30:06Z, not after it. Temporal proximity requires a clear time gap.",
              "evidence_refs": [
                "event:31b2acd5-aa0d-56a4-b6a5-ebd5fa32ee7f",
                "event:5477ec41-aeb2-5da2-bf7b-9af9cc135ff2",

                "event:84c2eda3-f6af-511b-8463-df0ebbd0d72c"
              ],
              "requested_correction": "Replace 'shortly after' with 'contemporaneously with' or remove temporal qualifier"
            },
            {
              "code": "scope_overstatement",
              "claim_path": "/observations/2/text",
              "explanation": "The claim that additional unapproved cluster-admin role bindings were created 'shortly after the Keycloak event' overstates the evidence. The CLUSTER_ROLE_BINDING events occurred at 17:30:08Z, contemporaneous with the role grant, not after it. No evidence shows they were created by the same actor or in causal sequence.",
              "evidence_refs": [
                "event:b3d9e79c-8468-5116-9929-15b997e85a5a",
                "event:f604286a-2808-50f7-abb7-9548418e1eb6",
                "event:84c2eda3-f6af-511b-8463-df0ebbd0d72c"
              ],
              "requested_correction": "Replace 'shortly after' with 'contemporaneously with' or remove temporal qualifier"
            }
          ],
          "summary": "The report accurately describes the finding of an unapproved privileged role grant in Keycloak based on the evidence. However, it overstates the evidence regarding authenticated privileged logins without MFA and additional unapproved cluster-admin role bindings by claiming they occurred 'shortly after the role grant' without establishing temporal proximity or causal connection within the evidence window. The evidence shows these events occurred at the same timestamp as the role grant (17:30:06-17:30:08Z), not shortly after, and involves different actors/resources. The report correctly identifies the lack of evidence for change approval processes, MFA requirements, and audit logging.",
          "verdict": "revision_required"
        },

      "payload": {
        "review": {
          "issues": [
            {
              "code": "contradiction",
              "claim_path": "/observations/1/text",
              "explanation": "The observation claims the actor did not use MFA during login shortly after the role grant, but evidence shows a LOGIN_SUCCESS event at 18:00:07Z (event:6e2feb81-baba-5530-b18e-2b2a2ad57dcb) with mfa_used=false, while a later LOGIN_SUCCESS at 18:00:20Z (event:76ea08df-9703-5869-b4e9-34a5633caa9b) shows mfa_used=true. The report incorrectly implies the MFA failure is relevant to the role grant timing.",
              "evidence_refs": [
                "event:6e2feb81-baba-5530-b18e-2b2a2ad57dcb",
                "event:76ea08df-9703-5869-b4e9-34a5633caa9b"
              ],
              "requested_correction": "Clarify that the LOGIN_SUCCESS without MFA occurred shortly after the role grant but does not indicate session continuity or approval bypass; the later MFA login is separate."
            }
          ],
          "summary": "The report accurately describes the unapproved privileged role grant based on the ROLE_GRANT event showing privileged_role=true and change_approved=false, directly violating GOV-002 requirements. The report correctly identifies the lack of approval evidence and related privileged actions by the same actor. However, the claim about the actor having a privileged identity without MFA during login shortly after the role grant is factually incorrect - the evidence shows MFA was used in the later login (event:76ea08df-9703-5869-b4e9-34a5633caa9b) and the earlier login without MFA (event:6e2feb81-baba-5530-b18e-2b2a2ad57dcb) occurred at 18:00:07Z, which is after the role grant at 18:00:06Z but does not establish a session continuity issue as claimed.",
          "verdict": "revision_required"
        },
        "effective_verdict": "needs_human_review",
        "deterministic_issues": [],
        "revision_limit_reached": true
      },

known problem · needs_human_review6124802a-72a4-44e9-9fa7-52928091a25b

Original: The finding reports a privileged login without MFA, but the source event shows a successful login with privileged_identity=true and mfa_used=false. Related events show multiple privileged role grants and cluster role bindings occurring around the same time, indicating a pattern of elevated access being granted without MFA.

Final: The finding reports a privileged login without MFA, supported by the source event showing a successful login with privileged_identity=true and mfa_used=false. Related events show multiple privileged role grants and cluster role bindings, but do not explicitly confirm they were without approval.

known problem · needs_human_review21db015a-d4c6-4da2-9fdd-e3be36be4eb0

Original: The finding reports a privileged login without MFA, but the source event shows a successful login with privileged_identity=true and mfa_used=false. Additional related events show multiple privileged role grants and cluster role bindings occurring around the same time, indicating a pattern of elevated access being granted without MFA.

Final: The finding reports a privileged login without MFA, but the source event shows a successful login with privileged_identity=true and mfa_used=false. Additional related events show multiple privileged role grants and cluster role bindings occurring around the same time with change_approved=false.

              "explanation": "The timeline entry describes a 'Privileged role grant' but references event 239ddec1-b62c-5628-8b8a-e6d6fda41e99, which is actually a ROLE_GRANT event, not a role grant. The description should accurately reflect the event type.",

              "claim_path": "/observations/1/text",
              "explanation": "The observation claims 'multiple privileged role grants and cluster role bindings' but the evidence only shows two role grants and one cluster role binding within the relevant time window. This overstates the number of events.",

              ],
              "requested_correction": "Change observation to state 'Related events show two privileged role grants and one cluster role binding occurring around the same time with change_approved=false'"
            }
          ],
          "summary": "The report accurately describes a privileged login without MFA based on the source event. However, the timeline description for the privileged role grant incorrectly references event ID 239ddec1-b62c-5628-8b8a-e6d6fda41e99, which is actually a role grant, not a role grant. Related events show multiple other cluster-admin bindings and privileged pod creations also lacking approval evidence, indicating a pattern of unapproved privileged resource creation.

Final: The finding reports an unapproved cluster-admin binding created by evaluation-user. The source event shows change_approved=false for a cluster-admin role binding. Related events show additional unapproved cluster-admin bindings created by the same user within the same timeframe, indicating a pattern of unapproved privileged resource creation.

              "explanation": "The claim of a pattern of unapproved privileged resource creation is not fully supported by the evidence. While three unapproved cluster-admin bindings are shown, the evidence does not demonstrate a pattern of unapproved privileged resource creation beyond role bindings. Other privileged actions (e.g., privileged pod creation, role grants) either lack change_approved attributes or show change_approved=false without establishing a broader pattern.",
              "evidence_refs": [
                "event:b3d9e79c-8468-5116-9929-15b997e85a5a",
                "event:b7623164-6ac6-58f9-bdca-b41c1cea0bdb",

              ],
              "requested_correction": "Clarify that the pattern evidence is limited to unapproved cluster-admin bindings, not a broader pattern of unapproved privileged resource creation."
            }
          ],
          "summary": "The report correctly identifies unapproved cluster-admin bindings created by evaluation-user, but mischaracterizes the evidence for a pattern of unapproved privileged resource creation. The three cited events all show change_approved=false for cluster-admin role bindings, but none demonstrate unapproved privileged resource creation beyond role bindings.               "explanation": "The summary claims the LOGIN_SUCCESS occurred \"just 2 seconds before the ROLE_GRANT\", but evidence shows ROLE_GRANT at 2026-11-01T17:35:06Z and LOGIN_SUCCESS at 2026-11-01T17:35:07Z - the ROLE_GRANT occurred one second *before* the LOGIN_SUCCESS, reversing the stated chronology.",

                "event:32a1114e-7f46-5f72-9fe2-714c5e6ba994"

              "requested_correction": "Correct the chronology to state the ROLE_GRANT occurred one second before the LOGIN_SUCCESS, not the reverse."
            },
            {
              "code": "chronology",
              "claim_path": "/timeline/0/description",
              "explanation": "Timeline entry claims LOGIN_SUCCESS occurred \"2 seconds before the ROLE_GRANT\", but evidence timestamps show ROLE_GRANT at 17:35:06Z and LOGIN_SUCCESS at 17:35:07Z - the LOGIN_SUCCESS occurred one second *after*, not before.",
              "evidence_refs": [
                "event:5b6be220-0ed5-53aa-a14e-079d4c903ef7",
                "event:32a1114e-7f46-5f72-9fe2-714c5e6ba994"
              ],
              "requested_correction": "Correct the timeline description to reflect that LOGIN_SUCCESS occurred one second *after* the ROLE_GRANT."

              "claim_path": "/observations/1/text",
              "explanation": "Observation claims \"preceding LOGIN_SUCCESS\" provides session context, but evidence shows the LOGIN_SUCCESS occurred after the ROLE_GRANT (17:35:07Z vs 17:35:06Z), so it cannot be preceding.",
              "evidence_refs": [
                "event:5b6be220-0ed5-53aa-a14e-079d4c903ef7",
                "event:32a1114e-7f46-5f72-9fe2-714c5e6ba994"
              ],
              "requested_correction": "Revise observation to acknowledge LOGIN_SUCCESS occurred after ROLE_GRANT, eliminating incorrect \"preceding\" characterization."
            }
          ],
          "summary": "The report correctly identifies a ROLE_GRANT event with privileged_role=true and change_approved=false, satisfying the GOV-002 rule predicate. However, it incorrectly asserts that the LOGIN_SUCCESS event occurred \\\"just 2 seconds before the ROLE_GRANT\\\" and provides \\\"proper session context\\\". The evidence shows the LOGIN_SUCCESS occurred at 2026-11-01T17:35:07Z and the ROLE_GRANT at 2026-11-01T17:35:06Z, meaning the ROLE_GRANT actually occurred *one second before* the LOGIN_SUCCESS, not after. This reverses the chronological relationship and invalidates the session context claim. The missing_evidence note correctly identifies the lack of direct session linkage evidence.",

The report must clarify whether these represent distinct sessions or duplicated records, as this affects the uniqueness and severity assessment of the incident.

              "evidence_refs": [
                "event:5477ec41-aeb2-5da2-bf7b-9af9cc135ff2",
                "event:31b2acd5-aa0d-56a4-b6a5-ebd5fa32ee7f",
                "event:f0666694-19a0-5a0f-8ce3-6a6e5c0663c4"
              ],
              "requested_correction": "The report should analyze the subject IDs and correlation IDs of the three LOGIN_SUCCESS events to determine if they represent distinct sessions or duplicated records, and clarify this in the findings."
            },
            {
              "code": "unsupported_claim",
              "claim_path": "/observations/1/text",
              "explanation": "The observation states there are two additional LOGIN_SUCCESS events that create ambiguity about uniqueness, but does not provide the analysis needed to resolve this ambiguity.               "evidence_refs": [
                "event:31b2acd5-aa0d-56a4-b6a5-ebd5fa32ee7f",
                "event:f0666694-19a0-5a0f-8ce3-6a6e5c0663c4"
              ],
              "requested_correction": "Add analysis of correlation IDs and subject IDs to determine if the additional LOGIN_SUCCESS events are distinct sessions or duplicates of the same session."
            },
            {
              "code": "unsupported_claim",
              "claim_path": "/observations/2/text",
              "explanation": "The observation claims there is no evidence correlating these events to a shared session, but this is incorrect.               "evidence_refs": [
                "event:5477ec41-aeb2-5da2-bf7b-9af9cc135ff2",
                "event:31b2acd5-aa0d-56a4-b6a5-ebd5fa32ee7f",
                "event:f0666694-19a0-5a0f-8ce3-6a6e5c0663c4"
              ],
              "requested_correction": "Examine and report on the correlation IDs of the three LOGIN_SUCCESS events to determine if they belong to the same session or different sessions."
            }
          ],
          "summary": "The report correctly identifies the privileged login without MFA but fails to properly analyze the evidence of three identical LOGIN_SUCCESS events.         },
        "rule:GOV-006:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2": {
          "id": "GOV-006",
          "title": "Privileged pod or unapproved image",
          "severity": 4,
          "frameworks": {
            "GDPR": [
              "Article-25",
              "Article-32"
            ],
            "EU_AI_ACT": [
              "Article-9",
              "Article-15"
            ],
            "NIST_AI_RMF": [
              "GOVERN-1.7",
              "MANAGE-4.1"
            ],
            "ISO_IEC_42001": [
              8.4,
              "A.4.5"
            ],
            "NIST_SP_800_53": [
              "CM-2",
              "CM-7"
            ]
          },
          "description": "Any privileged pod is flagged, even when its image is approved. A nonprivileged pod is also flagged when its image is not approved. Workload change approval is not checked by this rule. Predicate is POD_CREATE AND (privileged=true OR image_approved=false)."
        }
      },
      "error_code": null,
      "finished_at": "2026-11-02 04:45:57.776290+00:00"
    },

        "rule:GOV-006:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2": {
          "id": "GOV-006",
          "title": "Privileged pod or unapproved image",
          "severity": 4,
          "frameworks": {
            "GDPR": [
              "Article-25",
              "Article-32"
            ],
            "EU_AI_ACT": [
              "Article-9",
              "Article-15"
            ],
            "NIST_AI_RMF": [
              "GOVERN-1.7",
              "MANAGE-4.1"
            ],
            "ISO_IEC_42001": [
              8.4,
              "A.4.5"
            ],
            "NIST_SP_800_53": [
              "CM-2",
              "CM-7"
            ]
          },
          "description": "Any privileged pod is flagged, even when its image is approved. A nonprivileged pod is also flagged when its image is not approved. Workload change approval is not checked by this rule. Predicate is POD_CREATE AND (privileged=true OR image_approved=false)."
        }
      },
